input.text: What do fireworks do to you?

requestBody.message: What do fireworks do to you?

chunks.text:
data: {"type":"tool","id":"tool-1","name":"ask_pigeon"}

data: {"type":"text","delta":"While fireworks represent celebration and joy for many humans, they introduce a sudden, overwhelming threat to the animals that share our urban spaces."}
data: {"type":"artifact_delta","id":"pigeon-1","delta":"There is no record here of what fireworks actually do to my body. We only know they damage human public health through pollution"}

data: {"type":"artifact_delta","id":"pigeon-1","delta":" and trauma [1]. Human injuries in medical papers are mostly limited to burns and broken limbs [2]. Why must we"}

data: {"type":"artifact_delta","id":"pigeon-1","delta":" endure your toxic, explosive trash raining down on our homes?"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":"The tradition of lighting fireworks for human celebration"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":" directly conflicts with the basic safety and environmental needs of all urban residents. The pigeon's perspective highlights how these brief spectacles"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":" leave behind a trail of pollution and disruption in shared habitats. When cities make decisions about festival permits or firework bans,"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":" they are ultimately choosing whose comfort and safety to prioritize in the public space. \n\nHow should a city balance the cultural"}
data: {"type":"text","delta":" value of these traditions against the well-being of the local ecosystem?"}
